038/**
039 * Manages the lifecycles of {@link Coroutine}-based {@link Command Commands}. Commands may be
040 * scheduled directly using {@link #schedule(Command)}, or be bound to {@link Trigger Triggers} to
041 * automatically handle scheduling and cancellation based on internal or external events. User code
042 * is responsible for calling {@link #run()} periodically to update trigger conditions and execute
043 * scheduled commands. Most often, this is done by overriding {@link TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()} to
044 * include a call to {@code Scheduler.getDefault().run()}:
045 *
046 * <pre>{@code
047 * public class Robot extends TimedRobot {
048 *   @Override
049 *   public void robotPeriodic() {
050 *     // Update the scheduler on every loop
051 *     Scheduler.getDefault().run();
052 *   }
053 * }
054 * }</pre>
055 *
056 * <h2>Danger</h2>
057 *
058 * <p>The scheduler <i>must</i> be used in a single-threaded program. Commands must be scheduled and
059 * canceled by the same thread that runs the scheduler, and cannot be run in a virtual thread.
060 *
061 * <p><strong>Using the commands framework in a multithreaded environment can cause crashes in the
062 * Java virtual machine at any time, including on an official field during a match.</strong> The
063 * Java JIT compilers make assumptions that rely on coroutines being used on a single thread.
064 * Breaking those assumptions can cause incorrect JIT code to be generated with undefined behavior,
065 * potentially causing control issues or crashes deep in JIT-generated native code.
066 *
067 * <p><strong>Normal concurrency constructs like locks, atomic references, and synchronized blocks
068 * or methods cannot save you.</strong>
069 *
070 * <h2>Lifecycle</h2>
071 *
072 * <p>The {@link #run()} method runs six steps:
073 *
074 * <ol>
075 *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been scheduled
076 *       in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
077 *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
078 *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
079 *   <li>Call {@link #sideload(Consumer) periodic sideload functions}.
080 *   <li>Poll all registered triggers to queue and cancel commands.
081 *   <li>Queue default commands for any mechanisms without a running command. The queued commands
082 *       can be superseded by any manual scheduling or commands scheduled by triggers in the next
083 *       run.
084 *   <li>Start all queued commands. This happens after all triggers are checked in case multiple
085 *       commands with conflicting requirements are queued in the same update; the last command to
086 *       be queued takes precedence over the rest.
087 *   <li>Loop over all running commands, mounting and calling each in turn until they either exit or
088 *       call {@link Coroutine#yield()}. Commands run in the order in which they were scheduled.
089 * </ol>
090 *
091 * <h2>Telemetry</h2>
092 *
093 * <p>There are two mechanisms for telemetry for a scheduler. A protobuf serializer can be used to
094 * take a snapshot of a scheduler instance, and report what commands are queued (scheduled but have
095 * not yet started to run), commands that are running (along with timing data for each command), and
096 * total time spent in the most recent {@link #run()} call. However, it cannot detect one-shot
097 * commands that are scheduled, run, and complete all in a single {@code run()} invocation -
098 * effectively, commands that never call {@link Coroutine#yield()} are invisible.
099 *
100 * <p>A second telemetry mechanism is provided by {@link #addEventListener(Consumer)}. The scheduler
101 * will issue events to all registered listeners when certain events occur (see {@link
102 * SchedulerEvent} for all event types). These events are emitted immediately and can be used to
103 * detect lifecycle events for all commands, including one-shots that would be invisible to the
104 * protobuf serializer. However, it is up to the user to log those events themselves.
105 */
106public final class Scheduler implements ProtobufSerializable {
107  /**
108   * The default command bindings for each mechanism. Binding lists are ordered by priority; the
109   * last element in the list is the highest priority default command to be used. Bindings need to
110   * be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
111   */
112  private final Map<Mechanism, List<Binding>> m_defaultCommandBindings = new LinkedHashMap<>();
113
114  /**
115   * All bindings attached to this scheduler. This lets us cancel commands tied to scopes that go
116   * inactive. Bindings need to be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
117   */
118  private final Collection<Binding> m_activeBindings = new ArrayList<>();
119
120  /** Triggers with active command bindings that must not be allowed to be garbage collected. */
121  private final Set<Trigger> m_boundTriggers = new HashSet<>();
122
123  /** The set of commands scheduled since the start of the previous run. */
124  private final SequencedSet<CommandState> m_queuedToRun = new LinkedHashSet<>();
125
126  /**
127   * The states of all running commands (does not include on deck commands). We preserve insertion
128   * order to guarantee that child commands run after their parents.
129   */
130  private final SequencedMap<Command, CommandState> m_runningCommands = new LinkedHashMap<>();
131
132  /**
133   * The stack of currently executing commands. Child commands are pushed onto the stack and popped
134   * when they complete. Use {@link #currentState()} and {@link #currentCommand()} to get the
135   * currently executing command or its state.
136   */
137  private final Stack<CommandState> m_currentCommandAncestry = new Stack<>();
138
139  /** The periodic callbacks to run, outside of the command structure. */
140  private final List<PeriodicCallback> m_periodicCallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
141
142  /** Event loop for trigger bindings. */
143  private final EventLoop m_eventLoop = new EventLoop();
144
145  /** The scope for continuations to yield to. */
146  private final ContinuationScope m_scope = new ContinuationScope("coroutine commands");
147
148  /** Represents a single periodic callback. Stores a coroutine and its scope. */
149  private record PeriodicCallback(BindingScope scope, Coroutine coroutine) {}

189  /** Private constructor. Use static factory methods or the default scheduler instance. */
190  private Scheduler() {}

192  /**
193   * Sets the default command for a mechanism. The command must require that mechanism and cannot
194   * require any other mechanisms. If another default command has already been set for this
195   * mechanism, the one provided will supersede it.
196   *
197   * <p>If this is called inside a running opmode or in a running command, the default command
198   * setting will only apply while that opmode or command is active. When the opmode or command
199   * exits, the previous default command setting will be restored.
200   *
201   * <p>Commands running as default commands may call this method to change their mechanism's
202   * default command on the fly. The new default command will take effect at the end of the
203   * scheduler's loop cycle.
204   *
205   * @param mechanism the mechanism for which to set the default command
206   * @param defaultCommand the default command to execute on the mechanism
207   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the command does not meet the requirements for being a
208   *     default command
209   */
210  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
211  public void setDefaultCommand(Mechanism mechanism, Command defaultCommand) {
212    if (!defaultCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
213      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
214          "A mechanism's default command must require that mechanism");
215    }
216
217    if (defaultCommand.requirements().size() > 1) {
218      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
219          "A mechanism's default command cannot require other mechanisms");
220    }
221
222    var currentCommand = currentCommand();
223    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
224
225    var binding =
226        new Binding(
227            scope,
228            BindingType.CONTINUOUSLY_SCHEDULE_WHILE_HIGH,
229            defaultCommand,
230            new Throwable().getStackTrace());
231
232    var currentDefaultCommand = getDefaultCommandFor(mechanism);
233    m_defaultCommandBindings.computeIfAbsent(mechanism, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(binding);
234
235    if (currentCommand != null && currentCommand != currentDefaultCommand) {
236      // User called `setDefaultCommand` inside another command.
237      // Immediately reprocess the default commands for this mechanism to ensure it's in sync with
238      // the rest of the commands in the scheduler. This is required because we normally schedule
239      // the default commands at the start of the scheduler `run()` method, so the new default
240      // command wouldn't be handled until the next run (ie, the previous default command would
241      // still be active for the current iteration)
242      //
243      // Note that we cannot do this if the current default command is the caller because commands
244      // cannot be canceled while mounted.
245      processDefaultCommands(mechanism);
246    }
247  }
248
249  /**
250   * Gets the default command currently used for a mechanism.
251   *
252   * @param mechanism The mechanism
253   * @return The default command, or null if no default command was ever set
254   */
255  public Command getDefaultCommandFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
256    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
257    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
258      return null;
259    }
260
261    return bindings.getLast().command();
262  }
263
264  // package-private helper for unit test access
265  List<Binding> getDefaultCommandBindingsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
266    return m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
267  }

269  /**
270   * Adds a callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or control
271   * any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or LED
272   * data buffers), or perform some other helpful task. The callback is responsible for managing its
273   * own control flow and end conditions. If you want to run a single task periodically for the
274   * entire lifespan of the scheduler, use {@link #addPeriodic(Runnable)}.
275   *
276   * <p><strong>Note:</strong> Like commands, any loops in the callback must appropriately yield
277   * control back to the scheduler with {@link Coroutine#yield} or risk stalling your program in an
278   * unrecoverable infinite loop!
279   *
280   * <p>The coroutines provided to sideloaded functions will not cancel themselves if a fork or
281   * await call fails. This allows user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. You can opt
282   * into canceling the coroutine if a fork or await call fails by calling {@link
283   * Coroutine#setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)}.
284   *
285   * @param callback the callback to sideload
286   * @see #addPeriodic(Runnable)
287   */
288  public void sideload(Consumer<Coroutine> callback) {
289    var coroutine = new Coroutine(this, m_scope, callback);
290    // Sideloaded functions shouldn't be canceled if a command can't be forked. The default behavior
291    // should allow user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. This differs from
292    // coroutines issued to commands, which should fail by default to prevent unexpected robot state
293    coroutine.setCancelOnForkFailure(false);
294
295    var scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
296    m_periodicCallbacks.add(new PeriodicCallback(scope, coroutine));
297  }
298
299  /**
300   * Adds a periodic callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or
301   * control any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or
302   * LED data buffers), or perform some other helpful task.
303   *
304   * <p>For example:
305   *
306   * <pre>{@code
307   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
308   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> {
309   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("X", getX());
310   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("Y", getY());
311   * });
312   * }</pre>
313   *
314   * <p>{@code addPeriodic} is a convenience method that is identical to using {@link
315   * #sideload(Consumer)} with an unending {@code while} loop:
316   *
317   * <pre>{@code
318   * // An addPeriodic call:
319   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
320   *
321   * // Is equivalent to this sideload call:
322   * scheduler.sideload(coroutine -> {
323   *   while (true) {
324   *     leds.setData(ledDataBuffer)
325   *     coroutine.yield();
326   *   }
327   * });
328   * }</pre>
329   *
330   * @param callback the periodic function to run
331   * @see #sideload(Consumer)
332   */
333  public void addPeriodic(Runnable callback) {
334    sideload(
335        coroutine -> {
336          while (true) {
337            callback.run();
338            coroutine.yield();
339          }
340        });
341  }
342
343  /**
344   * Represents possible results of a command scheduling attempt. These can be used either as
345   * concrete results after a command was attempted to be scheduled, or as predictive results when
346   * checking if a command can be scheduled before committing to it.
347   */
348  public sealed interface ScheduleResult {
349    /**
350     * The command that was attempted to be scheduled.
351     *
352     * @return the command that was attempted to be scheduled
353     */
354    Command command();
355
356    /**
357     * Whether the scheduling attempt was successful.
358     *
359     * @return true if the scheduling attempt was successful, false if it failed
360     */
361    boolean successful();
362
363    /** Common interface for successful scheduling attempts. */
364    sealed interface Successful extends ScheduleResult {
365      @Override
366      default boolean successful() {
367        return true;
368      }
369    }
370
371    /** Common interface for failed scheduling attempts. */
372    sealed interface Failure extends ScheduleResult {
373      @Override
374      default boolean successful() {
375        return false;
376      }
377    }
378
379    /**
380     * A successful scheduling attempt.
381     *
382     * @param command the command that was successfully scheduled
383     */
384    record Success(Command command) implements Successful {
385      /**
386       * A successful scheduling attempt is always successful.
387       *
388       * @return true
389       */
390      @Override
391      public boolean successful() {
392        return true;
393      }
394    }
395
396    /**
397     * A scheduling attempt that was redundant because the command was already running.
398     *
399     * @param command the command that was attempted to be scheduled
400     */
401    record AlreadyRunning(Command command) implements Successful {
402      /**
403       * A scheduling attempt that was redundant because the command was already running is always
404       * successful.
405       *
406       * @return true
407       */
408      @Override
409      public boolean successful() {
410        return true;
411      }
412    }
413
414    /**
415     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a running
416     * command with shared requirements.
417     *
418     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
419     * @param alreadyRunning the running command that prevented the command from being scheduled
420     */
421    record LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(Command command, Command alreadyRunning)
422        implements Failure {}
423
424    /**
425     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a queued command
426     * with shared requirements.
427     *
428     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
429     * @param queuedCommand the queued command that prevented the command from being scheduled
430     */
431    record LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(Command command, Command queuedCommand)
432        implements Failure {}
433
434    /**
435     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the robot is in a disabled state and it requires one
436     * or more mechanisms that are not {@link Mechanism#controllableDuringDisabled() controllable
437     * during disabled}.
438     *
439     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
440     * @param unsafeMechanisms the uncontrollable mechanisms
441     */
442    record RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(Command command, Collection<Mechanism> unsafeMechanisms)
443        implements Failure {}
444  }
445
446  /**
447   * Checks if a command is able to be scheduled. Returns of the following states:
448   *
449   * <ul>
450   *   <li>{@link AlreadyRunning} if the command is already scheduled or running.
451   *   <li>{@link Success} if the command is not already scheduled or running and does not conflict
452   *       with any other scheduled or running commands.
453   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a
454   *       running command that shares requirements
455   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a queued
456   *       command that shares requirements
457   *   <li>{@link RequiresUnsafeMechanisms} if the command requires mechanisms that are not
458   *       controllable when the robot is disabled.
459   * </ul>
460   *
461   * @param command The command to check. Cannot be null.
462   * @return A schedule result indicating the schedulability of the command.
463   */
464  @NoDiscard
465  public ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Command command) {
466    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(command, "command", "isSchedulable");
467
468    if (isScheduledOrRunning(command)) {
469      return new AlreadyRunning(command);
470    }
471
472    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
473      var uncontrollables =
474          command.requirements().stream()
475              .filter(mechanism -> !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled())
476              .collect(Collectors.toSet());
477
478      if (!uncontrollables.isEmpty()) {
479        return new RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(command, uncontrollables);
480      }
481    }
482
483    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
484    for (var state = currentState(); state != null; state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
485      ancestry.add(state.command());
486    }
487
488    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
489  }
490
491  // similar to isSchedulable(Command), but used internally for processing bindings
492  // that may have command scopes.
493  private ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Binding binding) {
494    var command = binding.command();
495
496    if (isScheduledOrRunning(command)) {
497      return new AlreadyRunning(command);
498    }
499
500    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
501      var uncontrollables =
502          command.requirements().stream()
503              .filter(mechanism -> !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled())
504              .collect(Collectors.toSet());
505
506      if (!uncontrollables.isEmpty()) {
507        return new RequiresUnsafeMechanisms(command, uncontrollables);
508      }
509    }
510
511    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
512    if (binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand(Scheduler _, Command parent)) {
513      for (var state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
514          state != null;
515          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
516        ancestry.add(state.command());
517      }
518    } else {
519      for (var state = currentState();
520          state != null;
521          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
522        ancestry.add(state.command());
523      }
524    }
525
526    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
527  }
528
529  private Scheduler.ScheduleResult isSchedulableFromPriority(
530      Command command, Set<Command> ancestry) {
531    var running = m_runningCommands.values();
532    Command conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, running);
533    if (conflict != null) {
534      return new LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(command, conflict);
535    }
536
537    conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, m_queuedToRun);
538    if (conflict != null) {
539      return new LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(command, conflict);
540    }
541
542    return new Success(command);
543  }
544
545  /**
546   * Schedules a command to run. If one command schedules another (a "parent" and "child"), the
547   * child command will be canceled when the parent command completes. It is not possible to fork a
548   * child command and have it live longer than its parent.
549   *
550   * <p>Does nothing if the command is already scheduled or running, or requires at least one
551   * mechanism already used by a higher priority command.
552   *
553   * <p>For purposes of scheduling, a child command is considered to have a priority equal to the
554   * highest priority in its scheduling hierarchy. For example, if a parent command with priority 10
555   * schedules a child command with priority 5, the child command will be treated as having a
556   * priority of 10 and will interrupt any conflicting command with a priority of 10 or lower,
557   * rather than the usual 5.
558   *
559   * @param command the command to schedule
560   * @return the result of the scheduling attempt. See {@link ScheduleResult} for details.
561   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if scheduled by a command composition that has already
562   *     scheduled another command that shares at least one required mechanism
563   */
564  // Implementation detail: a child command will immediately start running when scheduled by a
565  // parent command, skipping the queue entirely. This avoids dead loop cycles where a parent
566  // schedules a child, appending it to the queue, then waits for the next cycle to pick it up and
567  // start it. With deeply nested commands, dead loops could quickly to add up and cause the
568  // innermost commands that actually _do_ something to start running hundreds of milliseconds after
569  // their root ancestor was scheduled.
570  public ScheduleResult schedule(Command command) {
571    // Get the narrowest binding scope.
572    // This prevents commands from outliving the opmodes that scheduled them, or from outliving
573    // their parents (eg if someone writes a command that manually calls schedule(Command) instead
574    // of using triggers to do so).
575    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
576
577    // Note: we use a throwable here instead of Thread.currentThread().getStackTrace() for easier
578    //       stack frame filtering and modification.
579    var binding =
580        new Binding(scope, BindingType.IMMEDIATE, command, new Throwable().getStackTrace());
581
582    return schedule(binding);
583  }
584
585  // Package-private for use by Trigger
586  ScheduleResult schedule(Binding binding) {
587    var command = binding.command();
588
589    var result = isSchedulable(binding);
590    if (!(result instanceof Success)) {
591      // We check specifically for Success, instead of `successful()`, because only a Success
592      // indicates that the command can actually go through the scheduling process. AlreadyRunning
593      // means what it says on the tin, and it would be incorrect to run the command back through
594      // the scheduling process.
595      return result;
596    }
597
598    if (!(binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand)) {
599      // Track this binding so we can disable it when it's out of scope.
600      // Note that, even though triggers can clean themselves up, commands that are manually
601      // scheduled cannot do the same, so we have to track them in the scheduler.
602
603      // We don't bother tracking command-scoped bindings; the bound command will already be
604      // cleaned up in the same cycle that the parent command exits, so this would attempt to
605      // double-cancel a child command across two cycles (once when the parent exits, and then in
606      // the next cycle in cancelStaleBindings). That would cause problems if the command object
607      // is immediately rescheduled as cancelStaleBindings would immediately cancel the new run
608      m_activeBindings.add(binding);
609    }
610
611    // Evict conflicting on-deck commands
612    // We check above if the input command is lower priority than any of these,
613    // so at this point we're guaranteed to be >= priority than anything already on deck
614    evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(command);
615
616    // If the binding is scoped to a particular command, that command is the parent. If we're in the
617    // middle of a run cycle and running commands, the parent is whatever command is currently
618    // running. Otherwise, there is no parent command.
619    var parentCommand =
620        binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand scope
621            ? scope.command()
622            : currentCommand();
623    var state = new CommandState(command, parentCommand, buildCoroutine(command), binding);
624
625    emitScheduledEvent(command);
626
627    if (currentState() != null) {
628      // Scheduling a child command while running. Start it immediately instead of waiting a full
629      // cycle. This prevents issues with deeply nested command groups taking many scheduler cycles
630      // to start running the commands that actually _do_ things
631      evictConflictingRunningCommands(state);
632      m_runningCommands.put(command, state);
633      runCommand(state);
634    } else {
635      // Scheduling outside a command, add it to the pending set. If it's not overridden by another
636      // conflicting command being scheduled in the same scheduler loop, it'll be promoted and
637      // start to run when #runCommands() is called
638      m_queuedToRun.add(state);
639    }
640
641    return result;
642  }
643
644  /**
645   * Checks if a command conflicts with and is a lower priority than any running command. Used when
646   * determining if the command can be scheduled.
647   *
648   * @return The conflicting command, or null if there is no conflict
649   */
650  private Command lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(
651      Command command, Collection<Command> ancestry, Collection<CommandState> checkAgainst) {
652    int maxAncestorPriority = command.priority();
653    for (Command ancestor : ancestry) {
654      maxAncestorPriority = Math.max(maxAncestorPriority, ancestor.priority());
655    }
656
657    // Check for conflicts with the commands that are already running
658    for (var state : checkAgainst) {
659      if (ancestry.contains(state.command())) {
660        // Can't conflict with an ancestor command
661        continue;
662      }
663
664      var c = state.command();
665      if (c.conflictsWith(command) && maxAncestorPriority < effectivePriority(state)) {
666        return c;
667      }
668    }
669
670    return null;
671  }
672
673  /**
674   * Calculates the effective priority of a command, taking into account the priorities of its
675   * ancestors.
676   *
677   * @param state The command state to check
678   * @return The effective priority of the command
679   */
680  private int effectivePriority(CommandState state) {
681    int max = state.command().priority();
682    for (var parent = state.parent(); parent != null; parent = state.parent()) {
683      state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
684      max = Math.max(max, parent.priority());
685    }
686    return max;
687  }
688
689  private void evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(Command command) {
690    for (var iterator = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
691      var scheduledState = iterator.next();
692      var scheduledCommand = scheduledState.command();
693      if (scheduledCommand.conflictsWith(command)) {
694        // Remove the lower priority conflicting command from the on deck commands.
695        // We don't need to call removeOrphanedChildren here because it hasn't started yet,
696        // meaning it hasn't had a chance to schedule any children
697        iterator.remove();
698        emitInterruptedEvent(scheduledCommand, command);
699        emitCanceledEvent(scheduledCommand);
700      }
701    }
702  }
703
704  /**
705   * Cancels all running commands with which an incoming state conflicts. Ancestor commands of the
706   * incoming state will not be canceled.
707   */
708  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
709  private void evictConflictingRunningCommands(CommandState incomingState) {
710    // The set of root states with which the incoming state conflicts but does not inherit from
711    Set<CommandState> conflictingRootStates =
712        m_runningCommands.values().stream()
713            .filter(state -> incomingState.command().conflictsWith(state.command()))
714            .filter(state -> !isAncestorOf(state.command(), incomingState))
715            .map(
716                state -> {
717                  // Find the highest level ancestor of the conflicting command from which the
718                  // incoming state does _not_ inherit. If they're totally unrelated, this will
719                  // get the very root ancestor; otherwise, it'll return a direct sibling of the
720                  // incoming command
721                  CommandState root = state;
722                  while (root.parent() != null && root.parent() != incomingState.parent()) {
723                    root = m_runningCommands.get(root.parent());
724                  }
725                  return root;
726                })
727            .collect(Collectors.toSet());
728
729    // Cancel the root commands
730    for (var conflictingState : conflictingRootStates) {
731      emitInterruptedEvent(conflictingState.command(), incomingState.command());
732      cancel(conflictingState.command());
733    }
734  }
735
736  /**
737   * Checks if a particular command is an ancestor of another.
738   *
739   * @param ancestor the potential ancestor for which to search
740   * @param state the state to check
741   * @return true if {@code ancestor} is the direct parent or indirect ancestor, false if not
742   */
743  @SuppressWarnings({"PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals", "PMD.SimplifyBooleanReturns"})
744  private boolean isAncestorOf(Command ancestor, CommandState state) {
745    if (state.parent() == null) {
746      // No parent, cannot inherit
747      return false;
748    }
749    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(ancestor)) {
750      // The given ancestor isn't running
751      return false;
752    }
753    if (state.parent() == ancestor) {
754      // Direct child
755      return true;
756    }
757    // Check if the command's parent inherits from the given ancestor
758    return m_runningCommands.values().stream()
759        .filter(s -> state.parent() == s.command())
760        .anyMatch(s -> isAncestorOf(ancestor, s));
761  }
762
763  /**
764   * Cancels a command and any other command scheduled by it. This occurs immediately and does not
765   * need to wait for a call to {@link #run()}. Any command that it scheduled will also be canceled
766   * to ensure commands within compositions do not continue to run.
767   *
768   * <p>This has no effect if the given command is not currently scheduled or running.
769   *
770   * @param command the command to cancel
771   */
772  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
773  public void cancel(Command command) {
774    var currentState = currentState();
775    if (currentState != null && command == currentState.command()) {
776      currentState.coroutine().requestCancellation(); // yields internally
777      return;
778    }
779
780    boolean running = isRunning(command);
781
782    // Evict the command. The next call to run() will schedule the default command for all its
783    // required mechanisms, unless another command requiring those mechanisms is scheduled between
784    // calling cancel() and calling run()
785    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
786    boolean queued = m_queuedToRun.removeIf(state -> state.command() == command);
787
788    if (running) {
789      // Only run the hooks if the command was running. If it was on deck or not
790      // even in the scheduler at the time, then there's nothing to do
791      // Always run onExit first, in case cancellation has special behavior that overrides
792      // standard exit logic.
793      command.onExit();
794      command.onCancel();
795    }
796
797    if (running || queued) {
798      // Emit a cancellation event only if the given command was in the scheduler
799      emitCanceledEvent(command);
800    }
801
802    // Clean up any orphaned child commands; their lifespan must not exceed the parent's
803    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
804  }
805
806  /**
807   * Updates the command scheduler. This will run operations in the following order:
808   *
809   * <ol>
810   *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been
811   *       scheduled in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
812   *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
813   *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
814   *   <li>Run sideloaded functions from {@link #sideload(Consumer)} and {@link
815   *       #addPeriodic(Runnable)}
816   *   <li>Update trigger bindings to queue and cancel bound commands
817   *   <li>Queue default commands for mechanisms that do not have a queued or running command
818   *   <li>Promote queued commands to the running set
819   *   <li>For every command in the running set, mount and run that command until it calls {@link
820   *       Coroutine#yield()} or exits
821   * </ol>
822   *
823   * <p>This method is intended to be called in a periodic loop like {@link
824   * TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()}
825   */
826  public void run() {
827    final long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
828
829    // Cancel any commands with stale binding scopes
830    cancelStaleBindings();
831
832    // Unbind any triggers with stale creation scopes.
833    // This allows triggers that can never be used again to be garbage collected to reduce
834    // memory usage and avoid potential OOMs from poorly written user code.
835    unbindStaleTriggers();
836
837    // If the robot is disabled, cancel any commands that require uncontrollable mechanisms
838    cancelCommandsThatCannotRunInDisabled();
839
840    // Sideloads may change some state that affects triggers. Run them first.
841    runPeriodicSideloads();
842
843    // Poll triggers next to schedule and cancel commands
844    m_eventLoop.poll();
845
846    // Schedule default commands for any mechanisms that don't have a running command and didn't
847    // have a new command scheduled by a sideload function or a trigger
848    scheduleDefaultCommands();
849
850    // Move all scheduled commands to the running set
851    promoteScheduledCommands();
852
853    // Run every command in order until they call Coroutine.yield() or exit
854    runCommands();
855
856    final long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
857    m_lastRunTimeMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
858  }
859
860  private void cancelStaleBindings() {
861    for (var iterator = m_activeBindings.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
862      var binding = iterator.next();
863      if (binding.scope().active()) {
864        continue;
865      }
866      cancel(binding.command());
867      iterator.remove();
868    }
869  }
870
871  private void unbindStaleTriggers() {
872    // Remove strong references to any triggers that have gone stale. This allows triggers to be
873    // garbage collected if they're not referenced outside the scope that created them. We don't
874    // clear any command bindings or unbind it from the event loop; otherwise, cached triggers
875    // would stop being updated until new command bindings are added.
876    for (var iterator = m_boundTriggers.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
877      var trigger = iterator.next();
878      if (!trigger.isScopeActive()) {
879        iterator.remove();
880      }
881    }
882  }
883
884  private void cancelCommandsThatCannotRunInDisabled() {
885    if (RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled()) {
886      // Nothing to do if the robot is enabled
887      return;
888    }
889
890    List<Command> commandsToCancel = new ArrayList<>();
891
892    for (var runningState : m_runningCommands.values()) {
893      var command = runningState.command();
894      boolean canRun = true;
895      for (var mechanism : command.requirements()) {
896        if (!mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
897          canRun = false;
898          break;
899        }
900      }
901
902      if (canRun) {
903        continue;
904      }
905
906      commandsToCancel.add(getRoot(command));
907    }
908
909    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
910      var command = queuedState.command();
911
912      boolean canRun = true;
913      for (var mechanism : command.requirements()) {
914        if (!mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
915          canRun = false;
916          break;
917        }
918      }
919
920      if (canRun) {
921        continue;
922      }
923
924      commandsToCancel.add(command);
925    }
926
927    for (var command : commandsToCancel) {
928      cancel(command);
929    }
930  }
931
932  /**
933   * Adds a bound trigger to this scheduler. The trigger will be unbound from the event loop when
934   * its creation scope becomes inactive and may be eligible for garbage collection.
935   */
936  // package-private for Trigger
937  void addBoundTrigger(Trigger trigger) {
938    m_boundTriggers.add(trigger);
939  }
940
941  /**
942   * Removes strong retention for a trigger, allowing it to potentially be garbage collected if no
943   * other references to it remain.
944   */
945  // package-private for Trigger
946  void removeBoundTrigger(Trigger trigger) {
947    m_boundTriggers.remove(trigger);
948  }
949
950  private void promoteScheduledCommands() {
951    // Clear any commands that conflict with the scheduled set
952    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
953      evictConflictingRunningCommands(queuedState);
954    }
955
956    // Move any scheduled commands to the running set
957    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
958      m_runningCommands.put(queuedState.command(), queuedState);
959    }
960
961    // Clear the set of on-deck commands,
962    // since we just put them all into the set of running commands
963    m_queuedToRun.clear();
964  }
965
966  private void runPeriodicSideloads() {
967    for (var iterator = m_periodicCallbacks.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
968      PeriodicCallback callback = iterator.next();
969      if (!callback.scope().active()) {
970        // The callback's enclosing scope exited - remove without running it and move on
971        iterator.remove();
972        continue;
973      }
974
975      // Update periodic callbacks
976      Coroutine coroutine = callback.coroutine();
977      coroutine.mount();
978      try {
979        coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
980      } finally {
981        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
982      }
983
984      if (coroutine.isDone()
985          || coroutine.isInterruptRequested()
986          || coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
987        // Callback finished or requested early termination - remove it from the list
988        iterator.remove();
989      }
990    }
991  }
992
993  private void runCommands() {
994    // TODO: Track command roots and run the commands in each root in reverse order, but run the
995    //       roots in insertion order
996    // Tick every command that hasn't been completed yet
997    // Run in reverse so parent commands can resume in the same loop cycle an awaited child command
998    // completes. Otherwise, parents could only resume on the next loop cycle, introducing a delay
999    // at every layer of nesting.
1000    for (var state : List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.values()).reversed()) {
1001      runCommand(state);
1002    }
1003  }
1004
1005  /**
1006   * Mounts and runs a command until it yields or exits.
1007   *
1008   * @param state The command state to run
1009   */
1010  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidCatchingGenericException")
1011  private void runCommand(CommandState state) {
1012    final var command = state.command();
1013    final var coroutine = state.coroutine();
1014
1015    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1016      // Probably canceled by an owning composition, do not run
1017      return;
1018    }
1019
1020    var previousState = currentState();
1021
1022    m_currentCommandAncestry.push(state);
1023    long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
1024    emitMountedEvent(command);
1025    coroutine.mount();
1026    try {
1027      coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
1028    } catch (RuntimeException e) {
1029      // Command encountered an uncaught exception.
1030      handleCommandException(state, e);
1031    } finally {
1032      long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
1033      double elapsedMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
1034      state.setLastRuntimeMs(elapsedMs);
1035
1036      if (state.equals(currentState())) {
1037        // Remove the command we just ran from the top of the stack
1038        m_currentCommandAncestry.pop();
1039      }
1040
1041      if (previousState != null) {
1042        // Remount the parent command, if there is one
1043        previousState.coroutine().mount();
1044      } else {
1045        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
1046      }
1047    }
1048
1049    if (coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
1050      cancel(command);
1051    } else if (coroutine.isDone()) {
1052      handleCommandCompletion(command);
1053    } else if (coroutine.isInterruptRequested()) {
1054      handleCoroutineIRQ(coroutine, command);
1055    } else {
1056      // Yielded
1057      emitYieldedEvent(command);
1058    }
1059  }
1060
1061  private void handleCommandCompletion(Command command) {
1062    command.onExit();
1063    emitCompletedEvent(command);
1064    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
1065    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
1066  }
1067
1068  private void handleCoroutineIRQ(Coroutine coroutine, Command command) {
1069    Command root = getRoot(command); // capture the root command before modifying scheduler state
1070    m_currentCommandAncestry.clear();
1071    emitForkFailureEvent(command, coroutine.getForkResult().getFailedCommands());
1072    cancel(root);
1073    Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
1074  }
1075
1076  /**
1077   * Handles uncaught runtime exceptions from a mounted and running command. The command's ancestor
1078   * and child commands will all be canceled and the exception's backtrace will be modified to
1079   * include the stack frames of the schedule call site.
1080   *
1081   * @param state The state of the command that encountered the exception.
1082   * @param e The exception that was thrown.
1083   * @throws RuntimeException rethrows the exception, with a modified backtrace pointing to the
1084   *     schedule site
1085   */
1086  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1087  private void handleCommandException(CommandState state, RuntimeException e) {
1088    var command = state.command();
1089
1090    // Fetch the root command
1091    // (needs to be done before removing the failed command from the running set)
1092    final Command root = getRoot(command);
1093
1094    // Remove it from the running set.
1095    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
1096
1097    // Intercept the exception, inject stack frames from the schedule site, and rethrow it
1098    var binding = state.binding();
1099    e.setStackTrace(CommandTraceHelper.modifyTrace(e.getStackTrace(), binding.frames()));
1100    emitCompletedWithErrorEvent(command, e);
1101
1102    // Clean up child commands after emitting the event so child Canceled events are emitted
1103    // after the parent's CompletedWithError
1104    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
1105
1106    // Bubble up to the root and cancel all commands between the root and this one
1107    // Note: Because we remove the command from the running set above, we still need to
1108    //       clean up all the failed command's children
1109    if (root != null && root != command) {
1110      cancel(root);
1111    }
1112
1113    // Then rethrow the exception
1114    throw e;
1115  }
1116
1117  /**
1118   * Gets the currently executing command state, or null if no command is currently executing.
1119   *
1120   * @return the currently executing command state
1121   */
1122  private CommandState currentState() {
1123    if (m_currentCommandAncestry.isEmpty()) {
1124      // Avoid EmptyStackException
1125      return null;
1126    }
1127
1128    return m_currentCommandAncestry.peek();
1129  }
1130
1131  /**
1132   * Gets the currently executing command, or null if no command is currently executing.
1133   *
1134   * @return the currently executing command
1135   */
1136  public Command currentCommand() {
1137    var state = currentState();
1138    if (state == null) {
1139      return null;
1140    }
1141
1142    return state.command();
1143  }
1144
1145  private void scheduleDefaultCommands() {
1146    m_defaultCommandBindings.keySet().forEach(this::processDefaultCommands);
1147  }
1148
1149  private void processDefaultCommands(Mechanism mechanism) {
1150    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.get(mechanism);
1151
1152    // Remove default command bindings that are no longer active.
1153    // If a default command is running when its scope goes inactive, also be sure to cancel it.
1154    bindings.removeIf(
1155        b -> {
1156          if (!b.scope().active()) {
1157            cancel(b.command());
1158            return true;
1159          }
1160          return false;
1161        });
1162
1163    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
1164      // Nothing to do. No active bindings remain.
1165      return;
1166    }
1167
1168    // Cancel any default command except the narrowest-scoped one (the last binding in the list)
1169    for (int i = 0; i < bindings.size() - 1; i++) {
1170      Command widerScopeDefaultCommand = bindings.get(i).command();
1171      cancel(widerScopeDefaultCommand);
1172    }
1173
1174    if (!RobotStateFetcher.getFetcher().isEnabled() && !mechanism.controllableDuringDisabled()) {
1175      // Default commands can never be scheduled if the robot is disabled and the mechanism is not
1176      // controllable during disabled, so there's no point in attempting to queue the default
1177      // command
1178      return;
1179    }
1180
1181    // Check if the mechanism is currently in use. We can queue the default command if it's not.
1182    for (Command runningCommand : m_runningCommands.keySet()) {
1183      if (runningCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
1184        return;
1185      }
1186    }
1187    for (CommandState queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
1188      if (queuedState.command().requires(mechanism)) {
1189        return;
1190      }
1191    }
1192
1193    // Nothing currently running or queued that needs this mechanism. Queue the default command.
1194    var defaultCommand = bindings.getLast();
1195    schedule(defaultCommand);
1196  }
1197
1198  /**
1199   * Removes all commands descended from a parent command. This is used to ensure that any command
1200   * scheduled within a composition or group cannot live longer than any ancestor.
1201   *
1202   * @param parent the root command whose descendants to remove from the scheduler
1203   */
1204  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1205  private void removeOrphanedChildren(Command parent) {
1206    m_runningCommands.entrySet().stream()
1207        .filter(e -> e.getValue().parent() == parent)
1208        .toList() // copy to an intermediate list to avoid concurrent modification
1209        .forEach(e -> cancel(e.getKey()));
1210  }
1211
1212  /**
1213   * Builds a coroutine object that the command will be bound to. The coroutine will be scoped to
1214   * this scheduler object and cannot be used by another scheduler instance.
1215   *
1216   * @param command the command for which to build a coroutine
1217   * @return the binding coroutine
1218   */
1219  private Coroutine buildCoroutine(Command command) {
1220    return new Coroutine(this, m_scope, command::run);
1221  }
1222
1223  /**
1224   * Checks if a command is currently running.
1225   *
1226   * @param command the command to check
1227   * @return true if the command is running, false if not
1228   */
1229  public boolean isRunning(Command command) {
1230    return m_runningCommands.containsKey(command);
1231  }
1232
1233  /**
1234   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, but is not yet running.
1235   *
1236   * @param command the command to check
1237   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run, false if not
1238   */
1239  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1240  public boolean isScheduled(Command command) {
1241    return m_queuedToRun.stream().anyMatch(state -> state.command() == command);
1242  }
1243
1244  /**
1245   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, or is already running.
1246   *
1247   * @param command the command to check
1248   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run or is already running, false if not
1249   */
1250  public boolean isScheduledOrRunning(Command command) {
1251    return isScheduled(command) || isRunning(command);
1252  }
1253
1254  /**
1255   * Gets the set of all currently running commands. Commands are returned in the order in which
1256   * they were scheduled. The returned set is read-only.
1257   *
1258   * @return the currently running commands
1259   */
1260  public Collection<Command> getRunningCommands() {
1261    return List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.keySet());
1262  }
1263
1264  /**
1265   * Gets all the currently running commands that require a particular mechanism. Commands are
1266   * returned in the order in which they were scheduled. The returned list is read-only.
1267   *
1268   * @param mechanism the mechanism to get the commands for
1269   * @return the currently running commands that require the mechanism.
1270   */
1271  public List<Command> getRunningCommandsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
1272    return m_runningCommands.keySet().stream()
1273        .filter(command -> command.requires(mechanism))
1274        .toList();
1275  }
1276
1277  /**
1278   * Cancels all currently running and scheduled commands. All default commands will be scheduled on
1279   * the next call to {@link #run()}, unless a higher priority command is scheduled or triggered
1280   * after {@code cancelAll()} is used.
1281   */
1282  public void cancelAll() {
1283    for (var onDeckIter = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); onDeckIter.hasNext(); ) {
1284      var state = onDeckIter.next();
1285      onDeckIter.remove();
1286      emitCanceledEvent(state.command());
1287    }
1288
1289    for (var liveIter = m_runningCommands.entrySet().iterator(); liveIter.hasNext(); ) {
1290      var entry = liveIter.next();
1291      liveIter.remove();
1292      Command canceledCommand = entry.getKey();
1293      // Always run onExit first, in case cancellation has special behavior that overrides
1294      // standard exit logic.
1295      canceledCommand.onExit();
1296      canceledCommand.onCancel();
1297      emitCanceledEvent(canceledCommand);
1298    }
1299  }
1300
1301  /**
1302   * An event loop used by the scheduler to poll triggers that schedule or cancel commands. This
1303   * event loop is always polled on every call to {@link #run()}. Custom event loops need to be
1304   * bound to this one for synchronicity with the scheduler; however, they can always be polled
1305   * manually before or after the call to {@link #run()}.
1306   *
1307   * @return the default event loop.
1308   */
1309  @NoDiscard
1310  public EventLoop getDefaultEventLoop() {
1311    return m_eventLoop;
1312  }
1313
1314  /**
1315   * For internal use.
1316   *
1317   * @return The commands that have been scheduled but not yet started.
1318   */
1319  @NoDiscard
1320  public Collection<Command> getQueuedCommands() {
1321    return m_queuedToRun.stream().map(CommandState::command).toList();
1322  }
1323
1324  private Command getRoot(Command command) {
1325    Command root = command;
1326    Command parent = getParentOf(command);
1327    while (parent != null) {
1328      root = parent;
1329      parent = getParentOf(parent);
1330    }
1331
1332    return root;
1333  }
1334
1335  /**
1336   * For internal use.
1337   *
1338   * @param command The command to check
1339   * @return The command that forked the provided command. Null if the command is not a child of
1340   *     another command.
1341   */
1342  public Command getParentOf(Command command) {
1343    var state = m_runningCommands.get(command);
1344    if (state == null) {
1345      return null;
1346    }
1347    return state.parent();
1348  }
1349
1350  /**
1351   * Gets how long a command took to run in the previous cycle. If the command is not currently
1352   * running, returns -1.
1353   *
1354   * @param command The command to check
1355   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command last took to execute.
1356   */
1357  public double lastCommandRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1358    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1359      return m_runningCommands.get(command).lastRuntimeMs();
1360    } else {
1361      return -1;
1362    }
1363  }
1364
1365  /**
1366   * Gets how long a command has taken to run, in aggregate, since it was most recently scheduled.
1367   * If the command is not currently running, returns -1.
1368   *
1369   * @param command The command to check
1370   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command has taken to execute in total
1371   */
1372  public double totalRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1373    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1374      return m_runningCommands.get(command).totalRuntimeMs();
1375    } else {
1376      // Not running; no data
1377      return -1;
1378    }
1379  }
1380
1381  /**
1382   * Gets the unique run id for a scheduled or running command. If the command is not currently
1383   * scheduled or running, this function returns {@code 0}.
1384   *
1385   * @param command The command to get the run ID for
1386   * @return The run of the command
1387   */
1388  @NoDiscard
1389  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1390  public int runId(Command command) {
1391    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1392      return m_runningCommands.get(command).id();
1393    }
1394
1395    // Check scheduled commands
1396    for (var scheduled : m_queuedToRun) {
1397      if (scheduled.command() == command) {
1398        return scheduled.id();
1399      }
1400    }
1401
1402    return 0;
1403  }
1404
1405  /**
1406   * Gets how long the scheduler took to process its most recent {@link #run()} invocation, in
1407   * milliseconds. Defaults to -1 if the scheduler has not yet run.
1408   *
1409   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the scheduler last took to execute.
1410   */
1411  @NoDiscard
1412  public double lastRuntimeMs() {
1413    return m_lastRunTimeMs;
1414  }

1416  // Event-base telemetry and helpers. The static factories are for convenience to automatically
1417  // set the timestamp instead of littering RobotController.getTime() everywhere.
1418
1419  private void emitScheduledEvent(Command command) {
1420    var event = new SchedulerEvent.Scheduled(command, RobotController.getTime());
1421    emitEvent(event);
1422  }

1459  /**
1460   * Adds a listener to handle events that are emitted by the scheduler. Events are emitted when
1461   * certain actions are taken by user code or by internal processing logic in the scheduler.
1462   * Listeners should take care to be quick, simple, and not schedule or cancel commands, as that
1463   * may cause inconsistent scheduler behavior or even cause a program crash.
1464   *
1465   * <p>Listeners are primarily expected to be for data logging and telemetry. In particular, a
1466   * one-shot command (one that never calls {@link Coroutine#yield()}) will never appear in the
1467   * standard protobuf telemetry because it is scheduled, runs, and finishes all in a single
1468   * scheduler cycle. However, {@link SchedulerEvent.Scheduled},{@link SchedulerEvent.Mounted}, and
1469   * {@link SchedulerEvent.Completed} events will be emitted corresponding to those actions, and
1470   * user code can listen for and log such events.
1471   *
1472   * @param listener The listener to add. Cannot be null.
1473   * @throws NullPointerException if given a null listener
1474   */
1475  public void addEventListener(Consumer<? super SchedulerEvent> listener) {
1476    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(listener, "listener", "addEventListener");
1477
1478    m_eventListeners.add(listener);
1479  }
1480
1481  private void emitEvent(SchedulerEvent event) {
1482    // TODO: Prevent listeners from interacting with the scheduler.
1483    //       Scheduling or canceling commands while the scheduler is processing will probably cause
1484    //       bugs in user code or even a program crash.
1485    for (var listener : m_eventListeners) {
1486      listener.accept(event);
1487    }
1488  }
1489}
